activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Homogeneous ODEs: Characteristic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.worked_solution:
Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}+49{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}+49) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}+49=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation has pure imaginary roots:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+49 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-49 \\ \lambda  & =\pm 7\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y=P\operatorname{cos}⁡7x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡7x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now let's find the constants $P$ and $Q.$ 

Substituting $y(0)=-2$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=-2.
$$

We now need to apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=7.$ First, we differentiate $y$ to find ${y}^{′}:$

$$
{y}^{′}=-7P\operatorname{sin}⁡7x+7Q\operatorname{cos}⁡7x
$$

Substituting ${y}^{′}(0)=7$ into the above gives

$$
7Q=7.
$$

So we have $P=-2$ and $Q=1.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
y=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡7x+\operatorname{sin}⁡7x.
$$
